issues.body: `COND_ATOMS` still accepts `!?inputs.<arbitrary-name>`, and `condition_is_live` checks only atom syntax and distinct paths. It does not consult either workflow's input declarations or admissible values. Consequently, changing the worker upload condition to `${{ !inputs.target_repo && steps.bundle.outcome == 'success' }}` is certified: both atoms match and their paths are distinct. But `target_repo` is a required non-empty string for admitted runs, so the upload is unreachable while the live ordering row still returns `ordered`. The added fixtures remain limited to language-level falsy values, duplicate paths, and wrapper syntax; none exercises a contradiction induced by the workflow input schema.
issues.fix_hint: Restrict accepted conditions to the exact known-live expressions used by the two upload steps, or validate input atoms and polarity against the workflow declarations and admitted values. Add a named negative fixture using `!inputs.target_repo` and assert `upload-step-disabled`; also demonstrate that mutating the live worker upload condition to that form makes the live assertion fail.
issues.title: Negated required inputs are still accepted as proven-live conditions

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

Round 4 leaves the round-3 blocker unchanged. `_upload_step_line` still accepts a negated arbitrary `inputs.<name>` solely because the path is syntactically distinct, without checking that the input can be falsy on an admitted run. Thus an upload can be made unreachable while `_seal_before_target_code` still reports `ordered`. No new negative fixture covers the workflow-input contract. The finding remains materially identical at blocker severity, so progress is stagnant.
